governance_matrix.decision_scope: Strategic and contractual decisions for the consortium: changes to the work plan, redistribution of resources between partners, changes in consortium composition, and amendments to the consortium agreement. The General Assembly is the final internal decision authority.
governance_matrix.meeting_frequency: Once a year, with extraordinary sessions convened at the coordinator's request.
governance_matrix.escalation_path: Unresolved matters remain with the General Assembly as the final internal authority. Contractual disputes are handled under the consortium agreement, which complements the grant agreement and contains no provision contrary to it.
source_basis: Tier 3 docs/tier3_project_instantiation/consortium/partners.json — all twelve partner_id values supply the composition.
Tier 1 governance_principles.json consortium_agreement_guidance — escalation wording tied to the rule that a consortium agreement complements and does not contradict the grant agreement.
governance_matrix.assumption_note: Body name and meeting frequency are not specified in Tier 3 and are not prescribed in Tier 1 extracted (no_prescribed_governance_body_names, no_prescribed_meeting_frequency). Both are selected as project-operational assumptions.

governance_matrix.decision_scope: Day-to-day operational management: cross-work-package coordination, monitoring of progress and deliverable quality, risk tracking, and preparation of decisions for the General Assembly. Members are the coordinator and the seven work-package leads.
governance_matrix.meeting_frequency: Quarterly, with additional calls when a risk or dependency requires one.
governance_matrix.escalation_path: Strategic, budgetary, or contractual matters that exceed operational management are referred to the General Assembly.

risk_register.description: The freshwater realm rests on one partner whose participation is unconfirmed
risk_register.mitigation: Identify a second freshwater partner before the grant agreement. If P07 does not join, the freshwater case is withdrawn and the second scope requirement is answered in two realms, not three. That is a scope change, not a delay, and the proposal states it rather than absorbing it. [Affects: WP4 (Demonstration and verification cases along the pressure gradient), WP5 (The omics and molecular observation layer)]

risk_register.description: The marine realm rests on one partner whose participation is unconfirmed
risk_register.mitigation: As R01. Losing P08 also removes the marine occurrence-record contribution of the cooperation duty, which P10 then carries alone for the terrestrial and freshwater records only. [Affects: WP4 (Demonstration and verification cases along the pressure gradient), WP3 (Joint protocols, metadata and interoperability crosswalks)]

risk_register.description: The consortium's geography is thin for a topic asking for use cases across Member States and Associated Countries
risk_register.mitigation: Ten of twelve partners sit in three country slots and five in C1. The composition condition survives losing any one gap partner, but the geographic spread the scope asks for does not. Broaden the user network and the stakeholder work across more countries before submission. [Affects: WP4 (Demonstration and verification cases along the pressure gradient), WP7 (Policy uptake, sectoral mainstreaming and exploitation)]

risk_register.description: The composition condition is met only under assumption
risk_register.mitigation: Every partner that adds a third country is fictional and Assumed. Confirm at least three independent beneficiaries in three countries, one of them in a Member State, before submission. The Joint Research Centre place is counted towards nothing. [Affects: WP1 (Coordination, governance and the interoperability interface)]

risk_register.description: No methodology vault backs the concept, so the mechanisms are design intent rather than source-grounded claims
risk_register.mitigation: Author the methodology before drafting Part B, so the Excellence section is lifted from evidence rather than from intent. Until then every mechanism claim carries Assumed and the drafting phases must not upgrade it. [Affects: WP2 (Knowledge gaps, data needs and the integration architecture), WP6 (Training resources, habitat mapping and trend prediction)]

risk_register.description: A joint protocol is agreed late, and a campaign runs under a protocol that changes afterwards
risk_register.mitigation: Milestone MS2 gates every campaign at M16. A campaign may not start before the protocol is delivered and adopted in writing by the partner running it. A protocol change after MS2 is a revision with its own record, not an edit. [Affects: WP3 (Joint protocols, metadata and interoperability crosswalks), WP4 (Demonstration and verification cases along the pressure gradient), WP5 (The omics and molecular observation layer)]

risk_register.description: The crosswalk between occurrence, habitat and ecosystem classifications does not resolve for some habitats
risk_register.mitigation: Report the unresolved labels rather than forcing a mapping. An unresolvable habitat is a finding the standards bodies need, and the contribution task exists to carry it to them. [Affects: WP3 (Joint protocols, metadata and interoperability crosswalks)]

risk_register.description: Environmental DNA reference libraries are incomplete for the taxa the cases need
risk_register.mitigation: Build reference sequences for the gap taxa inside the project, and report the share of reads that remained unassigned. An unassigned share is a result, not a failure, provided it is measured. [Affects: WP5 (The omics and molecular observation layer)]

risk_register.description: A field season is lost to weather, access or permitting in one of the three cases
risk_register.mitigation: Each campaign spans several annual cycles inside its window, so one lost season does not end a case. Secure site access and permits before the campaign starts, as part of the case selection dossier. [Affects: WP4 (Demonstration and verification cases along the pressure gradient)]

risk_register.description: The classification models learn the site rather than the biology
risk_register.mitigation: The split protocol is fixed in T6.2 before any model is trained, and site, season and treatment travel together into one fold. Benchmarks are reported under the declared split and under no other. [Affects: WP6 (Training resources, habitat mapping and trend prediction)]

risk_register.description: Practitioners do not act on the indicators the decision surface delivers
risk_register.mitigation: The usability evaluation asks whether a holding could act, not whether it liked the tool. A negative result is reported, because an indicator nobody acts on is the project's finding about the indicator. [Affects: WP7 (Policy uptake, sectoral mainstreaming and exploitation)]

risk_register.description: The budget arrives too late or inconsistent with the work package structure, and Phase 8 stays blocked
risk_register.mitigation: This is a lump-sum topic, so the repository computes no figure (CLAUDE.md §8.1). Prepare the budget request from the Phase 3, 4 and 6 outputs as soon as they are gated, and treat a missing response as a blocking gate failure rather than a hold state. [Affects: WP1 (Coordination, governance and the interoperability interface)]

risk_register.description: The satellite data the cases need is not available from the European programmes for a required band or revisit
risk_register.mitigation: The eligibility condition requires the European programmes to be used, and permits other data in addition. Record every additional source and the reason the European data did not cover the need. [Affects: WP4 (Demonstration and verification cases along the pressure gradient), WP6 (Training resources, habitat mapping and trend prediction)]

ethics_assessment.self_assessment_statement: The applicants complete the ethics self-assessment required for every Horizon Europe application, consistent with the Tier 1 rule that applicants must complete an ethics self-assessment as part of the application. The Tier 3 compliance_profile.json records ethics_review_required: false as a compliance flag derived during call binding; no Tier 2B extracted source path cites a mandatory ethics review as a topic-specific condition for this call. No human, human-embryo, human-cell, animal, or clinical ethics issue is identified for the planned biodiversity observation work at this stage. The project focuses exclusively on civil applications, consistent with the Tier 1 civil-focus constraint. Any personal-data processing is limited and is handled under the data protection and open science compliance task in WP1 (task T1.5). Integration of the gender dimension in research and innovation content follows the Tier 1 default rule that it is mandatory unless the topic explicitly states non-relevance. No Tier 2B exemption source is currently cited in this Phase 6 artifact; Phase 8 drafting must either add the relevant Tier 2B topic-source reference or keep the claim framed as pending call-specific confirmation. A gender equality plan is required at grant signature under the Tier 1 eligibility rule for public bodies, research organisations and higher education establishments in Member States and Associated Countries; the Tier 3 compliance_profile.json gender_plan_required flag is consistent with that rule. Should any ethics issue be triggered during implementation, the applicants will complete the ethics self-assessment in Part A Section 4 and provide an extended annex where needed.
